data: The Psychology of Sexuality and Gender

This course introduces students to social, economic, and political dimensions of gender and sexuality with the goal of understanding how the diversity of these two aspects of the human experience impacts psychology and its allied disciplines. We will take a multi-disciplinary approach to explore, in particular: (i) differences and interrelationships between sex, gender, and sexuality; (ii) the relevance of cultural contexts to understanding human variation, especially as regards family, subjectivity, the politics of identification, and the impact of the predominance of ‘WEIRD’ research; (iii) theories of the performative aspects of gender and sexuality and the relevance of labour to gender and sexual roles and identifications; (iv) problems of categorisation and classification of normalcy and pathology, contemporary views on variation in biology, and the historical legacies of pathologisation of women and gender and sexual minorities; (v) problems in the public circulation and communication of specialist research (including overgeneralisation and misrepresentation of scientific findings and clinical practice); and (vi) some contemporary approaches in psychology research and practice that build on these social understandings. Students will gain experience in understanding how gender and sexuality are operationalised in psychology and its related fields of psychiatry and social work in both research and practice, as well as the tools to critically evaluate the promises and limitations of individual research studies by considering them in these broader contexts.
